## Overview

Plan-Validate-Execute is a production workflow in three commands that extends native Plan Mode: `/plan-start`, `/plan-validate`, `/plan-execute`. Each run feeds an ADR learning loop that reduces human interruptions over time. Confidence: Tier 2, battle-tested by production teams shipping AI-first products at scale.

## The 3 commands

```bash
/plan-start    # PRD + dynamic research team + ADRs
/plan-validate # Structural checks + triggered specialist agents
/plan-execute  # Worktree + TDD + parallel execution + merged PR
```

Run `/clear` between each command: every command reads its inputs from disk (the plan file, ADRs), nothing needs to stay in context memory.

## /plan-start: 5-phase planning

| Phase | Content |
|-------|---------|
| 1. PRD & design | Missing/ambiguous requirements, compliance |
| 2. Technical | Explore agents, ADR creation for new decisions |
| 3. Scope | Research team selection (tier 0 to 4) |
| 4. Research | Agents run in parallel, `planning-coordinator` (Opus) synthesizes |

If 3+ confirmed ADRs already cover the decision, phase 2 auto-resolves with no agent.

## /plan-validate: 2-layer validation

Layer 1 (structural, instant): plan format, task ordering, ADR consistency. Layer 2 (specialists, 0 to 8 agents by risk): `security-reviewer`, `db-migration-reviewer`, `performance-reviewer`, among others, each triggered by a precise criterion (auth, schema migration, new route...).

Every issue must be resolved: auto-resolved from an existing ADR or `PATTERNS.md` entry, or settled by a human, which becomes a rule for next time.

## /plan-execute: to a merged PR

Isolated worktree, TDD scaffolding, parallel execution of independent tasks (commit per task), quality gate (tests + smoke test), PR and squash merge, worktree cleanup. If the quality gate fails: up to 3 auto-fix attempts by dedicated debug agents, then human notification.

## ADR learning loop

Every significant architectural decision generates an ADR. 1 ADR: watching. 2 ADRs: recommended default. 3+ ADRs: confirmed, auto-resolved on future plans, candidate for promotion to a hard rule in `CLAUDE.md`. On a 20-plan project, roughly 80% of architecture decisions auto-resolve.

## When to use this pipeline

| Criterion | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| Multi-layer feature (API + DB + UI) | Yes |
| Sensitive change (auth, payments, PII) | Yes |
| Typo, trivial refactor | No, native `/plan` is enough |
| Exploratory prototyping with unclear requirements | No |

## Cost

Typical Tier 2 feature: $2 to $10 for the full pipeline. Cost drops as ADR coverage grows: fewer agents needed, fewer validation issues, faster execution.

## Auto Plan Mode

Force native Plan Mode on all operations via `--append-system-prompt`:

```bash
alias claude-safe='claude --append-system-prompt \
  "$(cat ~/.claude/auto-plan-mode.txt)"'
```

The `auto-plan-mode.txt` file instructs Claude to present a plan and wait for explicit approval before each tool. Useful for sessions on critical or unfamiliar codebases, outside the 3-command pipeline.
